proposed_decisions.question: When the game side of the store moves to Die-Namic, what is apps/game?
proposed_decisions.commitment: the first engine, archived whole: Consus's AIGM (Jane GM, Engine Codex v1.5.0.0, engine_v1_7.py) kept unedited with its 2026-04-08 code review in https://github.com/rudi193-cmd/die-namic-games/tree/main/archive/first-engine, and apps/game becomes where Die-Namic is built, seeded empty
proposed_decisions.reason: apps/game is where Die-Namic's game master started, not one of its games: a Streamlit table run by Consus, 'your AIGM', the Die-Namic System's Generation Layer persona, on a 2d6 + stat roll read in three bands (ARCHITECT_ROLL, SUCCESS_STANDARD, CHAOS_BURST) over table stats that are AI-governance stats underneath (Grit, Weird, Cute, Cool as Integrity, Synthesis, Trust, Efficiency). Everything since descends from that roll: the-table's SceneSession rolls through Engine.roll today (avoiding the three methods that write engine_state.json, and swapping in a seeded stream for the global random), and willow's game-master rebuilt it on the record as strong / weak / miss, which the game box plays. 'stalled' in the catalog is true of the app (its review says it cannot run as-is) and false of the engine, which is load-bearing. Fixing it would rewrite the origin; keeping it whole keeps the lineage readable, and the-table's dependency intact.

proposed_rejections.question: May the one who runs the table win a roll without rolling?
proposed_rejections.option: the creator's roll always succeeds: Engine.roll in https://github.com/rudi193-cmd/die-namic-games/tree/main/archive/first-engine(stat, is_creator=True) returns 12 + the stat as an ARCHITECT_ROLL, and no dice are thrown
proposed_rejections.reason: it is the closed door every later piece answered. An authority that wins by fiat is the opposite of the covenant the game side kept from then on: the machine proposes and does not confirm (ai-game-master's CLAUDE.md), the dice are seeded by the record so nobody picks the faces, not even the one who rules the table (willow's dice, game-master), and the game master's power is a seal under a key, a ruling the table can see and check, never an outcome that skips the roll. The architect's always-win became the GM's seal.
